asConfiguredHint: With whatever balancing and redirects lie behind it — what a viewer gets.
browserCannotPlay: This browser cannot play HLS in a page.
bufferHint: How much is downloaded past the point being played.
chartBufferHint: How much is downloaded ahead of the point being played, and how far that point is behind the newest segment. A buffer that falls to zero is a stall.
chartDelay: Time of a segment by hop
chartDelayHint: Where the time of fetching one segment goes: waiting for the origin's first byte, downloading from it, waiting for the agent to take the request, the way from the agent to the server, the way from the server to this browser.
chartLossHint: Retransmissions are loss on the way from the agent to the server, counted by the agent, who sends. From the origin the monitor only receives, so loss on that way shows as segments arriving out of order — a sign of loss, not a count of it. The rest is what the player ran into.
chartLossShareHint: The share of TCP segments that had to be sent again, over the last half a minute, for every hop of the way. The one who sends counts: the vantage point on the way to the origin (these are its requests, not the video itself), the agent on the way to the server, the server on the way to your browser. There is no "Server → browser" line when a proxy stands between them: the server then sees the proxy's connection, not yours. Loss on the way from the origin to the vantage point cannot be counted — only segments out of order show there, on the chart next to this one.
chartRTTHint: To the origin and from the agent to the server: by the kernel's count on the connections in use (the smallest of the last half a minute at the agent), read on Linux only. Between the browser and the server: by the count of the server's kernel, and behind a proxy the browser times it itself — how long an empty request takes to be answered, the smallest of the last five.
chartRateHint: What the playlist declares for the quality being played, and what the segments really take: their size over their duration.
chartSpeed: Download speed of a segment, by hop
chartSpeedHint: The size of a segment over the whole time it took on the hop, waiting for the answer included. This is not traffic: a segment is fetched in a burst and then nothing is fetched until the next one, so on a fast network the speed is many times the bitrate. What matters is that every hop stays above the bitrate; a hop that falls to it cannot keep up with the stream. A segment that passed a hop in less than 20 ms is too small to tell a speed by: there is no point for it.
codecNotSupported: The browser cannot decode what the stream carries
droppedHint: Frames the browser did not show in time. Says more about this computer than about the stream.
latencyHint: How far the point being played is behind the newest segment of the playlist.
lead: The stream as the monitor sees it: the server, or one of its agents, requests playlists and segments from where it makes its checks, and they are passed to this page. Ask the stream's own address, or one particular server behind it.
lineOutOfOrder: Out of order from the origin
passedOn: {asked} did not serve the stream itself: it passed the request on to {got}.
playlistCannotBeParsed: The playlist could not be parsed by the player
playlistTimedOut: The playlist did not arrive in time
ranOutOfBuffer: Playback stalled: the buffer ran out
segmentCannotBeParsed: A segment could not be parsed by the player
segmentTimedOut: A segment did not arrive in time
serverNotSeenHint: Asked directly, past the balancer. This server is known from other streams and may not have this one.
serverSeenHint: Asked directly, past the balancer. It last answered for this stream {ago}.
title: Watch
unsupportedHint: The browser has no decoder for this stream. H.264 video with AAC audio plays everywhere; MPEG-2 video, AC-3 audio and HEVC depend on the browser and the system. This says nothing about the stream itself.
vantageAgentHint: The agent requests the stream from where it stands and hands it over to the server: browser → server → agent → origin.
vantageServerHint: The server itself requests the stream.
